text: ABOUT THE SERIES Theoretical Astrophysics, Step by Step Theoretical Astrophysics, Step by Step is a Japanese–English series for learning the shared tools of astrophysics. It pairs foundations through school algebra with an advanced volume using differential equations. VOLUME I16 lessons available Foundations Exploring the universe through school algebra Light and distance, quantum physics and radiation, stars and their limits, and cosmic expansion—one algebraic step at a time. Open the foundations ↗ VOLUME II35 worked chapters available Advanced Equilibrium, instability, transport, and similarity solutions Lane–Emden, collapse, cluster relaxation, rotating ellipsoids, alpha disks, and Toomre Q—a path toward learning through equations. View chapters and learning guide ↗ Foundations: exploring the universe through school algebra All 16 lessons, questions, references, and four interactive panels are available. No differential equations are solved. The optional entropy-maximization extension uses derivatives. Supplied laws from quantum mechanics and relativity are distinguished from the algebra developed here. Advanced: equilibrium, instability, transport, and similarity solutions 35 worked chapters are available in a 35-topic learning guide, covering cloud equilibrium, gravitational instability, cosmic structure, spherical accretion and winds, disk transport, MRI, Toomre Q, fluid interfaces, shocks, radiation, and ionization. Each topic shows its publication status. Supplement: numbers and units The supplement covers pc, h and ℏ, electron rest mass, solar mass, H₀, the fine-structure constant, G, and c. Compare values and equations in SI and Gaussian CGS. Open numbers and units ↗ Further reading Find standard references on galactic dynamics, radiation, stellar structure and evolution, cosmology, compact objects and fluid stability, plus PP III reviews on star and planet formation. Each entry includes preparation and connections to this site. Open the reading guide ↗ Teaching principles Astrophysical phenomena are the focus. Equations of state, opacities, and recombination coefficients are used with their meaning and validity stated; microscopic material-property derivations are not a separate theme. Connect intuition, assumptions, algebra, and questions. Distinguish estimates, exact results, and supplied coefficients, stating their conditions. Build advanced chapters in three stages: understand the phenomenon, formulate the equations, and solve and check. Plot provenance and validation The figures are conceptual illustrations or teaching plots recomputed from theoretical models. Checks against known solutions and conservation laws are distinct from reproducing a specific paper figure. A figure comparison requires its number, physical conditions, axes, normalization, and data scope. The same place in two languages Language switching keeps the current chapter and expanded syllabus entries. Language and completion records stay in your browser.
